title: An interval exchange transformation all of whose connection times are finite is periodic
source_title: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Interval exchange transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An IET is a piecewise translation of an interval determined by a permutation of the subintervals; the endpoints of the subintervals are its discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the map studied in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Connection time
standard_prerequisites.statement: M(beta) is the first return time of the left endpoint of the subinterval beta to the set of discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis is that all these times are finite, which is what makes the orbit set of discontinuities finite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Poincare recurrence
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a finite measure preserving transformation every measurable set of positive measure recurs.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the return time N of the partition element.

core_obligations: Show that the hypothesis makes the set of all forward and backward iterates of the discontinuities finite, and take the partition generated by those points (source lines 196-200).

For an element of that partition, show that every iterate of the transformation acts continuously on it, by arguing that a discontinuity of an iterate would have to lie in the image of the element, contrary to the choice of the partition (source line 202).

Use recurrence to find a return time of the element to itself, and show that the image of the element under that iterate equals the element itself, using again the choice of the partition to exclude the two remaining possibilities (source lines 204-208).
Conclude that the iterate is the identity on the element, so that the orbit is periodic on each element and the interval decomposes into finitely many periodic components (source line 210).

proof_roadmap.step: Finiteness of the orbit set of the discontinuities and the induced partition.
Each iterate acts continuously on each partition element.
Recurrence plus the partition choice force exact return of the element.
The returning iterate is a piecewise translation fixing the element, hence the identity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 191-193: if for every subinterval except one the connection time is finite, then the interval exchange transformation has only periodic orbits, with a finite decomposition into periodic components on which the period is uniform. The proof (source lines 195-211) uses three ingredients that the statement does not mention: the orbit set of the discontinuities is finite under the hypothesis, so it generates a finite partition; every iterate acts continuously on each element of that partition, because a discontinuity of an iterate would have to be an image of a partition point; and Poincare recurrence supplies a return time whose return is exact, the two other possibilities being excluded by the choice of the partition. Only then does the argument conclude that a power of the transformation fixes an element on which it is a piecewise translation.
